title: New image dataset aims to improve AI-based navigation of PV cleaning robots
content:
Researchers have created a dataset of 6,200 solar panel images designed to support AI-based navigation of cleaning robots. The dataset features annotated panel reference lines under clean, synthetically soiled, and laboratory contamination conditions, with the aim of helping developers assess the robustness of visual navigation algorithms.

title: Octopus Energy unveils heat pump add-on for home cooling
content:
K-based Octopus Energy has introduced Cosy Cooler, a hydronic cooling unit designed to work with its existing Cosy heat pumps. The company says the device can be installed using existing radiator pipework and will cost between GBP 500 ($670) and GBP 600 when it becomes available in 2027.

title: Dutch startup offers PV mounting solution for fragile roofs
content:
Dutch startup Rable has developed a self-supporting PV mounting system for fragile roofs with slopes of up to 10 degrees, reducing anchor points by 95% compared with conventional systems. The galvanized-steel structure distributes loads of 6 kg/m² to 15 kg/m² and can reduce installation costs by €0.15 ($0.16)/W, according to the company.

content:

title: Saudi Arabia uses 250 MW solar park to breed threatened gazelles
content:
Saudi Arabia’s Prince Mohammed bin Salman Royal Reserve has introduced 38 Sand gazelles into an operational solar facility following a seven-month trial. The project aims to use existing PV infrastructure as a breeding habitat for threatened wildlife, with the first births expected this winter.

title: Germany deploys 12.76 GW of solar in first nine months of 2026
content:
Germany installed 1.23 GW of solar capacity in September, down from 1.64 GW in August, as utility-scale additions hit their lowest level of 2026 and rooftop demand remained weak. Despite the slowdown, installations in the first nine months of 2026 reached 12.76 GW, slightly above the same period last year.

content:

title: Finland demands grid-forming support for new wind, solar in weak grids
content:
Fingrid will require new wind and solar plants in Finland’s weakest grid areas to provide grid-forming capability, which developers can meet with co-located batteries sized at up to 30% of plant output.

title: Mova launches residential battery with integrated EV charging management
content:
The Mova LumeGret S5000 residential energy storage system combines solar power management, expandable battery storage, and electric vehicle charging. The system supports up to 4.8 kW of solar input and can be paired with a 7 kW EV charger.

title: Scientists develop moth-eye-inspired antireflective surfaces for PV modules
content:
Researchers in Portugal have investigated the mechanical durability of moth-eye-inspired antireflective silicon surfaces for photovoltaic applications. They found that repeated sliding causes nanopillar fracture and material compaction, with higher mechanical loads leading to increased friction and wear.

title: Meter socket adapters are approved by 86 utilities across 33 states

title: Grid inertia is the new reliability

content: The standalone battery energy storage system will be the largest on the East Coast and is expected to reach commercial operations in late 2027 to deliver critical capacity to the Boston area grid.

title: Texas to account for almost half of domestic U.S. silicon module production in 2027
content: Texas is projected to produce over 45% of U.S. silicon-based solar modules in 2027 within 100 miles of the I-45 corridor, driven by rapid multi-gigawatt facility deployment and pro-business incentives according to Terawatt PV Research.

title: Company that put gas engines in Teslas goes bankrupt owing $37 million
content: Obrist, the Austrian engineering firm famous for ripping battery cells out of a Tesla Model 3 and bolting a gas engine into the frunk, is bankrupt. Three companies in the Obrist Group are insolvent with combined debts of about €31.8 million, or roughly $37 million.

title: BMW’s new i3 just drove 753 miles on a single charge
content: BMW put the new i3 to the test to showcase the power of its Gen6 batteries. The long-wheelbase i3 covered 753 miles (1,213 km) without stopping, the longest covered by any BMW EV to date.
